concept: Bombay Cafe Map x Javaphile Worli: a logo-first, two-ink risograph reel. The real Bombay Cafe Map lockup opens as the hook, a letter-O reveal drops into the 3D island-to-Worli zoom, and every scene keeps the lockup as a top bar until the big end-card lockup.

dimensions.palette: cobalt blue ink, chartreuse ink, bone paper, overprint dark where inks cross (no orange, no cream)
dimensions.fonts: variable-weight grotesk headlines + IBM Plex Mono labels, two faces only
dimensions.opening: logo-first: the real Bombay Cafe Map lockup printed in one cobalt ink holds large, then settles into the top bar as a letter-O reveal opens the Mumbai island and zooms into Worli
dimensions.transition: continuous letter-O reveal: the next scene is already inside the growing counter of the O (no blank frame), 12 frames
dimensions.camera: parallax layers with slow drift, one hard dolly-in on the facade
dimensions.layout: magazine grid: asymmetric boxes of image, number and text
motion_device: coffee pour fills the grid cell
dimensions.texture: risograph overprint with grain and 3D extruded map
dimensions.sound: slow calm voice (Kokoro 0.5, at most 2.2 words/s, 0.4 s air), cafe foley, soft pad with a light pluck
dimensions.ending: stacked Bombay Cafe Map lockup with @bombaycafemap and bombaycafemap.com, the cafe name, and the question, held 3 s+

experiment.hypothesis: A two-ink overprint look with visible misregistration feels printed and calm for a quiet cafe, and avoids the Claude-orange/cream and the teal-ink look of Mary Lodge.
